title: The English word "constructor" makes Jarvis's rules throw, so the sentence gets no answer
what_happens: normalise() checks words with `tok in LOAN` and `tok in EN_NUM`, plain objects, so "constructor" is found on Object.prototype and the Object function goes into the tokens. normalise("show the constructor").text is "show the function Object() { [native code] }", and understand() then throws TypeError: tok.startsWith is not a function. Thunai.tsx calls understand with no try: typed, handle() rejects after the ribbon shows the sentence, and no reply comes (Thunai.tsx:1166). Heard by captions, the throw comes out of fromCaptions (conductor.ts:248). Heard by Whisper, it lands in the catch at conductor.ts:295, which reads it as 'Whisper is not reachable' and turns on the browser captions fallback. That gate runs on overheard speech too, so someone in the room saying the word is enough. The last three steps are read from the code; the throw itself is run.
what_should_happen: "constructor" is a word like any other. It stays a word in the tokens, and the sentence goes on to the planner.
repro: npx vitest run --config vitest.qa4.config.ts tests/qa/pass4/scans-code.test.ts (tests named scans-code-1, written with it.fails). Patch: use Object.hasOwn(LOAN, tok) and Object.hasOwn(EN_NUM, tok), or make both a Map.
class: plain object used as a lookup: Object.prototype names count as found

title: A sign-in saved for the picker is never removed, even after the dataset is deleted
what_happens: When a link with an API key or password holds several datasets, ingestLink saves <token>.auth (the sign-in and browser session, encrypted) and <token>.pick.json.gz (what was read with that sign-in, gzip only). ingestPick copies the sign-in to the new dataset's id. deleteDataset and deleteConnector remove only that id's files. Nothing removes the token's files: dropVault, the one function made to remove a sign-in, has no caller, and no code deletes .pick.json.gz. In the test, after the dataset is deleted getVault(token) still returns the sign-in and both files are still there. A picker that is opened and walked away from leaves the same two files, while store.ts:121 says a dataset that was never kept leaves nothing behind.
what_should_happen: After the Collector deletes a connected dataset no copy of its sign-in, or of the data read with it, stays on disk. An abandoned picker's files go too.
repro: npx vitest run --config vitest.qa4.config.ts tests/qa/pass4/scans-code.test.ts (tests named scans-code-4: the real ingestLink and ingestPick against the local fixture server, a temporary STUDIO_DIR and a made-up key). Patch: drop the token's .auth and .pick.json.gz by age (say 24 hours) in the scheduler and when the picker's queue ends. They cannot simply go after the first pick, because Studio.tsx adds several datasets from one token one after another.
class: dead safety function: clean-up nobody calls

title: The number gate treats the word "constructor" as a spoken figure and refuses the line
what_happens: figuresIn reads EN_WORDS[w] from a plain object, and EN_WORDS["constructor"] is the Object function, not undefined. So figuresIn("The constructor has not finished the drain.") returns one figure, gateChunk says not ok, fillTemplate returns null and spellsNumber says true. A line with no number in it gets refused as if it held one. It fails safe (no wrong number is spoken), but the line is lost.
what_should_happen: No figure is found in that sentence, and the line passes.
repro: npx vitest run --config vitest.qa4.config.ts tests/qa/pass4/scans-code.test.ts (tests named scans-code-2). Patch: Object.hasOwn(EN_WORDS, w) and Object.hasOwn(TG_WORDS, w).
class: plain object used as a lookup: Object.prototype names count as found

area: Collector and officer APIs: period filter
title: ?period=constructor passes the check: the overview answers 500 and the export comes back empty
what_happens: parsePeriod uses `v in PERIODS`, so constructor, __proto__, toString and valueOf are all accepted as periods. PERIODS[period].hours is then undefined. On the pinned snapshot: periodSince, kpiBlock, overview and report throw RangeError: Invalid time value, so those routes answer 500, and overview also leaves an unhandled rejection in the log, because kpiBlock is already running when another entry in the same array throws. exportRows does not throw: it returns 0 rows where daily returns 42, so the export route would answer 200 with an empty file. Only someone signed in can reach this, by editing the address; the app's own screens never send such a value. The data functions were run directly; the routes were read, not called, because this job had no server port.
what_should_happen: Any unknown period falls back to daily, as parsePeriod("nonsense") already does.
repro: npx vitest run --config vitest.qa4.config.ts tests/qa/pass4/scans-code.test.ts (tests named scans-code-3). Patch: typeof v === "string" && Object.hasOwn(PERIODS, v).
class: `in` operator on a plain object used as input validation

title: Status changes never reach the live dataset files: the function for it has no caller
what_happens: src/lib/dataset/append.ts says later status changes add lines to grievance_status_history.csv, and appendStatusChangeToDataset says to call it after every status update (Officer and Collector APIs). No code calls it; only POST /api/complaints appends, at filing. So the history file holds filing-time rows until someone runs npm run dataset:export by hand. Nothing in production reads these files (only scripts do), which is why this is not rated higher.
what_should_happen: Either the status routes call it, or the comments and the function go, and the docs say the files are refreshed only by dataset:export.
repro: node tests/qa/pass4/prod-reach.cjs | grep appendStatusChangeToDataset (listed as nobody), and search src/ for the name: only its own definition.

title: npm run lint has never worked: there is no ESLint config, and running it changes tsconfig.json
what_happens: next lint stops at its set-up prompt, exits 1, and adds a line to tsconfig.json's include (restored at once in this run). next.config.js also sets ignoreDuringBuilds, so nothing lints the code. A report-only run with next/core-web-vitals found 0 rules-of-hooks errors, 6 exhaustive-deps warnings (read, none shown to cause a bug), 6 no-img-element and 1 no-unescaped-entities (AskOverlay.tsx:78).
what_should_happen: npm run lint runs without a prompt and without touching tracked files.
repro: npx next lint < /dev/null (then git checkout -- tsconfig.json). Report-only run: npx eslint --no-eslintrc -c tests/qa/pass4/eslintrc.scan.json --ext .ts,.tsx src. Patch: add .eslintrc.json with {"extends": "next/core-web-vitals"}, and add the @typescript-eslint plugin too, because 24 inline disable comments name its rules.
root_cause_guess: chennai-grievance-portal-main/package.json script lint; no ESLint config file

title: One dead file and 87 dead names; the safety-named ones were checked and their job is done elsewhere
what_happens: src/components/AuthHeroPanel.tsx is imported by nothing. 87 top-level names outside the test-only modules are reached by neither production, tests nor scripts. Safety-named ones checked one by one: requireRole, getResendCooldown (createOtp enforces the cooldown itself), gateB (resolve.ts uses earns directly), isStage, verifySmtp, PASSWORD_RULES. Dead screens: FreshWarn (replaced by the Collected chip), FromDatasets in BriefingBook.tsx, AddSource in Sources.tsx, FeedsBody, six officer cards in Cards.tsx, four helpers in reportPdf.ts, and the voice chooser functions in mouth.ts and voice.ts. Knip also lists 500-odd exports and types as unused, but most are used inside their own file, so only the export word is spare; those are not worth a change. Aliases: encryptSecret and decryptSecret are deliberate names for the Aadhaar functions; isStopOnly is unused.
what_should_happen: Removed when convenient. Nothing here changes what a user sees.

title: Some green tests guard code production never runs, and one copy has already drifted
what_happens: These are tested but production never calls them: followUpMoves (camera.ts:154), insightsFor (map/insights.ts:32; ask.ts:313 always sets insights to an empty list), storyAI (studio/ai.ts:149), attention (studio/drill.ts:103), replyLanguage (assistant/lang.ts:109), grainFor (assistant/limits.ts:85; compile.ts:385 has its own copy), joinable (catalog.ts:461), matchesAll (searchwords.ts:41, by design a copy of the SQL rule). followUpMoves has drifted: its test says a "chip" edit always moves the camera, while useMapAsk.ts:209 keeps the view when the shape is the same. Also, src/lib/thunai/rules.ts, which qa.live.ts and holdout.live.ts use to score sentences 'via rules', is never loaded in production, so that score goes through a hand-written lane order, not the production one. Whether the two orders differ was not checked.
what_should_happen: Production calls the tested function, or the test and the copy go.
repro: node tests/qa/pass4/prod-reach.cjs (the lines marked tests); compare camera.test.ts:80-81 with useMapAsk.ts:209
class: test guards a copy, not the real path

title: animejs is unused; three scripts rely on packages not in package.json
what_happens: animejs is a production dependency no file imports. jiti (build-embeddings.cjs, build-lance.cjs, eval-assistant.cjs), fast-png (build-elevation.mjs) and fflate (build-transit-layer.mjs) are not listed; they resolve only because tailwindcss, vite and jspdf bring them. The scripts call require("jiti")(...), the version 1 form, and knip already brings jiti 2 nested, so a change in which version is hoisted would break embed:build, lance:build and eval:assistant. Knip's other flags are not findings: word-list and @huggingface/transformers are loaded by path, and the remaining dev tools are this QA pass's own.
what_should_happen: animejs removed; jiti (at ^1), fast-png and fflate listed as devDependencies.
repro: npx knip --config tests/qa/pass4/knip.json --no-exit-code; npm ls jiti fast-png fflate --depth=2
